messages:
devon: Heads-up — private VPC tenant `acme-telemetry` in eu-west1 just saturated their reserved GPU pool. p95 gen latency jumped to 12s and our queue length metric hit 780. Can we push a short oncall playbook for customer-side throttling?

maria: Ack. Seen the spike on the dashboard. GPUs at ~98% util, swap activity on hosts rising. Customers report intermittent 429s. Need immediate mitigations + guidance for longer-term config.

aj: Quick mitigations we can recommend to customers right now: lower client concurrency, enable jittered exponential backoff, and add a cheap fallback model. 

sasha: For specifics: recommend per-instance inflight limit = 6 for large models, queue depth = 12. If the customer needs lower-latency SLOs, drop inflight to 2-4. Also add a local request queue with a hard cap so they fail fast instead of piling up.

leo: +1. Sample token-bucket config we should share: 
```
# token-bucket: refill 10 tokens/sec, burst 30
max_tokens: 30
refill_rate_per_sec: 10
cost_per_request: 1
```
Clients consume 1 token per request; this keeps short bursts but enforces steady QPS.

devon: Important: distinguish 429 vs 503 guidance in the playbook. Recommend customers treat 429 as client-rate signal and backoff, while 503 indicates system overload or transient infra where retry-after should be respected. We push Retry-After header on 503s where we have an estimate.

maria: Add these practical rules to the doc: 
- Retry policy: exponential backoff with full jitter (base=200ms, cap=10s, factor=2).
- Max retries: 3.
- Respect `Retry-After` if present.
- Fall back to a quantized/smaller model variant after 2 failed retries for non-critical requests.

aj: Also propose health-check endpoint polling to adapt client behavior, e.g.:
```
GET /v1/health?model=gpt-small
200 {"available_slots": 4, "queue_len": 6}
```
If available_slots <= 0, clients should reduce concurrency and queue or route to fallback.

sasha: Telemetry knobs to collect on customer side: in_flight, latency_p50/95/99, retries, retry_after_seen, fallback_rate. We'll ask them to ship these as tags in logs so we can correlate with infra metrics.

leo: For Envoy/nginx customers, example rate-limit config snippets to include: 
- Envoy token bucket filter with `max_tokens` set to reserved QPS.
- nginx `limit_req_zone` with burst and nodelay turned off to avoid head-of-line stalls.

oncall-bot: Incident note created: INC-20260312-789. Affected tenant: acme-telemetry. Priority P2. Assigned to devon/sasha.

devon: Longer-term advice for customers on dedicated/private deployments: 
- Provision a small buffer of burst capacity if they expect periodic spikes (reserved + small burst pool).
- Use auto-scale rules tied to queue_len and host_util > 85% for n minutes, but cap cost by budget window.
- Prefer warm pools for large models (keep one warm instance per region) to avoid cold-start latencies.

maria: Cost tradeoffs we should put in the guide: cheaper fallback (quantized or 8-bit) reduces GPU cost and latency; acceptance of lower quality should be explicit via feature flag. Also document how burst capacity increases monthly bill and where to set hard caps.

aj: Add a small library snippet for client-side admission control (pseudocode):
```
if in_flight >= MAX_INFLIGHT or queue.len >= MAX_QUEUE:
  return 429 "client_throttled"
else:
  enqueue(request)
```
This forces fail-fast behavior.

sasha: One operational tip: ask customers to expose a `X-Client-Concurrency` header so our support team can quickly see client-side config in traces. Also recommend `X-Model-Fallback` when serving a degraded model.

devon: Cool. I'll assemble a short runnable playbook and paste it into the customer KB: immediate steps, sample configs (Envoy/nginx/token-bucket), recommended retry/backoff, health-check patterns, and metrics to collect. Will also include a checklist for us (support + infra) to adjust burst pools if the tenant's business case warrants it.

maria: Thanks — please ping when the KB is ready and we can send a concise checklist to the customer CSM. :thumbsup:
